language.script_notes: Place names carry heavy Native American and colonial-English roots (e.g. Massachusetts, Concord).

road_furniture.bollard_color: Mostly absent, delineator posts where used.
road_furniture.curb_style: Dense old-town cores with granite curbs (especially in Massachusetts); narrow, often winding roads that predate the automobile grid seen further west.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Dry-stacked fieldstone walls running along roadsides through wooded and pasture land are a very strong New England-specific tell (a legacy of colonial-era farm clearing).

architecture.roof_style: Steep-pitched gable roofs on colonial and Federal-style houses; gambrel (barn-style) roofs also common.
architecture.roof_material: Wood shingle/shake on older historic homes.
architecture.wall_construction: White clapboard wood siding is the classic New England look; red brick rowhouses and townhouses common in older Mid-Atlantic cities (Philadelphia, Baltimore); dry-stacked stone walls lining fields and roads.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White/pale clapboard with black shutters is the iconic New England palette; red brick in Mid-Atlantic urban cores.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: White clapboard colonial houses with black shutters; New England town greens with a white church steeple; triple-decker houses in Massachusetts mill towns; brownstone rowhouses in New York/Philadelphia.

nature.vegetation: Dense deciduous hardwood forest (maple, oak, birch) — famous for autumn foliage; mixed with white pine.
nature.terrain: Rolling hills and low mountains (Appalachians, Green/White Mountains), a rocky Atlantic coastline in Maine, dense urban corridor from Boston to Washington D.C.
nature.climate_signature: Four distinct seasons, often overcast/rainy in imagery, snow in winter, vivid orange/red foliage in fall.

vehicles.plate_color: Varies by state within the region — Massachusetts red-on-white, New York blue-and-gold, Pennsylvania blue-and-yellow, Vermont green-and-white.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Higher Subaru presence than the national average given hilly/snowy terrain; otherwise standard national fleet.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations, generally newer/higher quality in and around the dense Boston–NYC–DC corridor.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense coverage given high population density; rural Maine/Vermont/New Hampshire have thinner coverage than the urban corridor.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Deciduous forest, brick architecture in older towns, similar four-season climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Northeast has dry-stacked stone walls, narrower pre-automobile road layouts, and hillier terrain; the Midwest is flatter with a much more regular grid road pattern and more farmland.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar deciduous forest, colonial-era architecture, rocky coastline in Maine vs. the Maritimes
confusion_set.tiebreaker: US plates carry a state name (not a Canadian province), yellow center lines and mph speed signage; French bilingual signage appears in Quebec but not New England.
